# ADJUDICATION METHOD — p370's rule, not HEAD equality.  p370 established that "a HEAD sha is
# not an identity proof" and re-derives identity on the REF-SET FINGERPRINT: the sha256 of the
# sorted (sha, ref) pairs of a full `git ls-remote --symref`.  All ten addresses were probed
# first-hand on 2026-10-22 and the ten .refs captures are committed under
# compose/code/p370-refset-register/refsets/.

column2: dasgltd/mcp-brasil and mcp-brasil/mcp-brasil share a HEAD (2efb258370b1) and have DIFFERENT REF SETS — 52 refs against 101.  They are two distinct repositories that currently agree at the tip, which is exactly the fork case gate-identity-online's own recipe comment warns about: "two genuinely distinct forks share a HEAD on the day one is forked from the other."

column1: why_it_matters
column2: Had this pass adjudicated on HEAD — the only evidence the gate itself prints — it would have written a FALSE alias into the register and taught every successor that one of these two addresses is a stale name for the other.  🟢 p370's instrument refused it on evidence the gate does not collect.  An instrument built two passes ago caught the pass that was running it.

column1: latam_note
column2: 🔵 And the refused pair is the LATAM one.  mcp-brasil is this base's thinnest region; collapsing two Brazilian addresses into one would have cost a region that has 1 agent row.

column1: # 🔴 THE SECOND FINDING, which is about this base rather than about GitHub.
systemic
column2: 🔴 THE PATTERN IS SYSTEMIC, not one lapse.  Across this base's history at least FIVE address identities were PROVEN FIRST-HAND and written into prose — p348's wallet specimen, the openedx rename, and the two owner transfers above, plus the inginious pair that WAS registered — and before this pass aliases.tsv held TWO rows.  🔵 The register is the only form a successor's instrument can read; prose is the form only a reader can.

column1: p348_specimen
column2: digitalcredentials/learner-credential-wallet + openwallet-foundation-labs/learner-credential-wallet is the pair NAMED IN p348's OWN DOCSTRING as the specimen that motivated building the gate — "ONE repository, published twice, under owners that share no characters."  p348 proved it, wrote it into its prose, and never added it to aliases.tsv.  🔵 Nine passes later the gate it built found its own example unregistered, because nobody could run the gate.  A finding filed in PROSE and not in a REGISTER is a finding this base loses — the same class as p372's "the one address with a proven successor had been proven six days earlier and filed only in prose".

column1: # 🔴 WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, stated rather than promoted to agree.
direction_limit
column2: For three of the four registered pairs the canonical DIRECTION is NOT first-hand.  raw.githubusercontent.com serves BOTH names with a 200 (GitHub follows the rename redirect on the raw channel too), and api.github.com answers 403 from here, so no channel available to this pass distinguishes the old name from the new.  The direction recorded for the IMS Global/1EdTech, DCC/OpenWallet and pytorch/meta-pytorch pairs rests on the organisations' published renames — secondary attribution — and is labelled as such in the register.

column1: direction_established
column2: openedx/edx-platform -> openedx/openedx-platform is the one direction with a named source: discuss.openedx.org's own rename announcement ("Renaming edx-platform to openedx-platform on Jan 26").  TIER-1 ISSUER on p377's outlet scale: the project's own forum.

column1: raw_channel_result
column2: 🔵 A useful null for a successor: the raw channel CANNOT be used as a canonicality oracle.  Both sides of all four renamed pairs return 200, and openedx returns 404 on both sides (no README.md at the probed path).  Recorded so no successor re-derives it.
